source_claims.claim: For a martingale X_n and stopping time T, E[X_T] = E[X_0] when one of the three stated optional-stopping conditions holds.
Under the alternatives, T is finite almost surely, so X_T is well-defined almost surely and finite stopped processes converge pointwise to the stopped value.
Theorem 13.17 supplies E[X^T_n] = E[X_0] for every finite n.
Case (i): if T is almost surely bounded by C, then X_T agrees almost surely with the stopped process at C and E[X_T] = E[X_C^T] = E[X_0].
Case (ii): if T is finite almost surely and |X_n| is uniformly bounded by K, dominated convergence gives lim_n E[X^T_n] = E[X_T].
Case (iii): if E[T] is finite and increments are uniformly bounded by c, the telescoping estimate gives an integrable dominator |X_0| + cT, so dominated convergence gives lim_n E[X^T_n] = E[X_T].
The canonical version constructs X_T internally instead of requiring an arbitrary representative.
